Question: What happens on TV all the time, but never happens in real life?
Answer: Turning on the news at the perfect moment Has this ever happened to you: You suspect the police is looking for you. You turn on the TV. At that exact moment, on that exact channel, there is a picture of you and a news anchor urging people to “be on the lookout for this dangerous suspect”? If your answer is yes, then you may be a movie character. Getting info on specific topics by randomly turning on the news never happens in real life, yet is a very common movie trope. So common in fact that even making fun of it has become widespread. Take this Arrested Development scene for instance: Michael: Don’t tell me Gob is not in Iraq. Jarvis: Oh no Michael, he’s there. In fact, he’s on the news! (Turns on TV. There is a commercial break) Jarvis: I’m sure it’s coming right up…any minute now. … Jarvis: Right after this series of adds, it’s been on all day. Assistant: Why don’t we just go online? Jarvis: Cool you Japanese jets, it’s coming. (TV finally talks about Gob) Jarvis: AHA! Now imagine the impact if that had come on right when we turned on the TV!

Name: Michael Strauss
Question: What was the worst twist in a film, show, book, etc.?
Answer: Little nightmares 2 This 2021 Tarsier Studios production is a delightful horror adventure game, featuring a wholesome story of friendship and camaraderie, a fascinatingly grotesque and well crafted horror setting, and one of the worst, most rage inducing twists I’ve ever seen in an otherwise great video game. A twist so nonsensical, it ruins the entire heart of the story and kills all replay value. *SPOILERS AHOY* You start the game playing as Mono. A little boy with a paper bag on his head, waking up in a bizarre and twisted world, where every shadow hides something that wants you dead. Early in the game, rummaging through the creepy cabin of a deranged, slasher movie style huntsman, you encounter Six. It’s not sure if she’s a prisoner or just another lost child, but she is hiding under a table, scared and desperate to get out. You extend a helping hand, starting a beautiful friendship that will serve as a security blanket in the midst of the horror that’s still to come. A little glimmer of light to push through the madness dominating this disturbing world. Together you escape the lunatics cabin, relying on each other to solve little puzzles, access places otherwise unreachable, and handling objects made for the giant inhabitants of this place. Together you run away, but end up having to navigate one horrifying, skin crawling scenario after another. A creepy elementary school, ran by the horror version of Dolores Umbridge. A hospital full of zombie like mannequins that move in the shadows and freeze when you shine a light on them. Like those creepy things in Doctor Who. All the while, Mono and Six having each others back. Helping to cross ledges, opening doors, saving each others lives countless times. Hand in hand, overcoming everything this horrid world throws at them. Eventually, the big bad of the game comes along: The Thin Man. His presence causes Mono to have a seizure and he kidnaps Six, taking her away to a giant TV tower. A signal is broadcasted here, which seems to be the source of the twisted force that controls the world. Unnaturally bending it to the Thin Man’s will. Snapping out of his seizure, Mono goes straight after her. He eventually defeats the Thin Man, with some previously unknown telekinetic abilities, and reaches her enclosure. He finds her a twisted abomination, corrupted just like the rest of the world. Call me a wuss all you want, it broke my heart to see her like this. Not giving up, Mono finds the source of corruption: the music box she holds in her hands. He manages to destroy it, all the while avoiding her mad swings, and gets her back to normal. As soon as that happens, the tower starts collapsing. The ground is shaking, the ceilings are falling, and our two reunited heroes dash for the exit. They reach a ledge with a gap in it. The exit is just beyond. Safety is mere steps away. Six makes the jump. Mono is unable to, but as he jumps, Six reaches out and catches his hand. The same way she did many many many times before. Only this time, she does not help him up. Yep. She drops him to his death. Or to whatever horror awaits him at the bottom of that fall. The end. So, why do I say this is the stupidest twist I’ve ever encountered? Is it because I was invested in the two, and desperately wanted to see them riding off into the sunset? Partly, yes…but that’s not the main reason. The main reason is it makes no sense! They spent so much time literally risking their lives for each other, and now she just drops him? After she just let herself get captured to help him? After he just came for her and saved her from a fate worse than death? It makes absolutely no sense. Here’s how I imagine the conversation in the production team went. The game was 95% complete, and then some guy decided: Creative hack: ”Holy crap, we have no dark twist for the end! I really want something cool and shocking, let’s have her drop Mono!” Normal writer: “Um…that makes no sense. Everything we did up to this point is the exact opposite of what you’re suggesting.” Creative hack: “It doesn’t matter, I want a twist. It’ll be cool, come on.” Normal writer: “A twist needs proper foreshadowing, we haven’t set anything up. You can’t just throw it in there out of the blue.” Creative hack: “Do it or I’m telling my dad” (takes another huff of paint) There is speculation online from people reaching far and wide to make it make sense. However you slice it though, it’s just cheap shock for the sake of shock. One explanation claims that in the final scene, Six saw Mono’s face for the first time and he kind of looked like the Thin Man, so she dropped him. Nevermind that he just saved her life for the bazillionth time, she didn’t like his face. I would have preferred they both die at the hands of the Thin Man, or in the crashing building. That would at least make sense. It bugs me to no end. The developers managed to create something great up to that point. They offered a beautiful, real message that’s at the heart of so many great stories: the world is full of madness and horror, but can be navigated through friendship, love and compassion. A wonderful premise, ruined for the sake of cheap shock value.

Name: Michael Strauss
Question: What is the most deceiving thing about fitness?
Answer: How simple it is This impressive looking specimen is Danish bodybuilder and fitness model Martin Valentin Larsen. Looking at him, many would assume he got his physique by a combination of Viking blood with some special training regime. A dozen different techniques, a down to the second routine that requires military grade logistic and a bunch of special equipment reserved for the one percenters. In this video he talks about building and maintaining a six pack, and reveals how deceptively simple fitness is at it’s core. He spends the entire video describing the cable crunches exercise and then wraps it up. Honestly, it’s the only exercise I use. There’s no secret. It’s just one good exercise, and that’s it. You have to be committed to eating clean and get low in your body fat. That’s it. That’s fitness. Commit to a routine and eat well. There’s no secret. No special exercises that “target that stubborn belly fat” or “particular timing for ingesting protein” to be concerned with. The internet is so full of “secret” advice on workout routines, splits, tempos, nutrition, supplements, breathing techniques and so much more that it’s easy for a newcomer to get choice paralysis. Truth is, most of that is just influencers trying to stand out from the competition with some whacky new hook. Sure, there are ways to optimize your fitness journey. The bottom line however, the basis of it all is commitment to some form of exercise and eating healthy. You don’t need a spotter, a barbell, a bench, sunglasses and leather pants to do abs, like Lenny Kravitz. To clarify, when I say fitness is “simple” I don’t mean it’s easy. I mean anyone can get started at any time. That being said, committing to working out and eating clean can be hard at the beginning. The good news is, it gets easier.

Name: Michael Strauss
Question: Can you name an example of bad parenting?
Answer: “We never say ‘no’ to our child. Whatever he wants to do, that’s what we do” our guests said, as their two year old was trying to climb on the dinner table, swinging his spoon at the lamp hanging above. “He will eventually realize we are being kind to him. He will appreciate it and return the favor” “Aaaaaha. Riiiiight” I thought, as I pointed the kid to some toys, hoping he will go play and let us have a few minutes of adult conversation. He got off the chair and started pulling my sleeve, asking me to go play with him. I throw a desperate look at our guests, hoping they will intervene. They look back at me smiling, completely oblivious that not everyone wants to have their entire Friday evening decided on by a toddler. “Hahaha, now you have to go play with him, that’s so cute”. It felt like in that one episode of The Twilight Zone. After some time, the two year old master of the family decided everyone should be watching cartoons. In the middle of dinner, our “kind parenting” guests got up to move to the couch. All three of them singing cringey songs and pointing out various animals for the next hour or so. As soon as they left, my wife and I looked at each other, took an exhausted sigh of relief and decided to never have them over again. I understand being kind to your kids, letting them explore and feeding their curiosity. I’m all for that. But to not impose any boundary at all? Is he raising himself? I’m not saying he should sit quietly on a chair the whole time but…maybe just watch cartoons by yourself for 30 minutes while the adults can have a chat? How is that kid going to react when he gets out into the world and not everyone is bending over backwards to his every whim? How will he learn to compromise and coexist with other kids who have their own needs and wants? Or with society as a whole? You can’t let a two year old call the shots in the house. It’s not good for them, and it’s not good for you either. You’ll go nuts.

Name: Michael Strauss
Question: Do you agree with George R.R. Martin that it was a mistake for Tolkien to bring Gandalf back as Gandalf the White because Gandalf's sacrifice to save the Fellowship was the most poignant moment and momentous plot development in The Lord of the Rings?
Answer: Nope Killing off Gandalf would have made for an interesting story, but not in the hands of Tolkien. G.R.R. Martin on the other hand, would do great with that premise. I understand why he would suggest it. That’s his particular way of creating character arks. Jamie Lannister is the best swordsman in the land? Let’s cut off his right hand and see what he does now. Tyrion Lannister’s biggest obstacle is his unfortunate physical appearance? Let’s chop off his nose too and see how he copes with this one. Daenerys Targaryen’s stability comes from her marriage with Khal Drogo? Whack him. Let’s see how she carries on. Theon Greyjoy’s entire personality is to be a womanizing party guy? Wonder what he does without his pork sausage. In the same spirit, Martin looked at The Lord of the Rings, saw that Gandalf was the one with all the answers and asked himself “how would they handle things without him?” That’s just his way of creating conflict. Of giving his characters something to overcome. It’s a great formula, but it’s specific to him. I does not fit in Tolkien’s hands. The Lord of The Rings, as described by Tolkien himself, is “a fundamentally religious and Catholic work”. Enlightenment trough self sacrifice for the greater good is a central Christian theme. Gandalf the Grey falls, and Gandalf the White comes back. There can be no other way.

Name: Michael Strauss
Question: What are some examples of well-written female protagonists? What makes them strong female characters?
Answer: Toda Mariko - Shogun “I’ve always considered women to be people” - George R.R. Martin when asked how he’s able to write good female characters. Women are not an alien race. The secret is the same as writing any strong character. Their development should follows a simple formula: a flawed individual, who rises above an insurmountable obstacle in order to serve a cause greater than herself. While the recent activist takeover of certain studios in Hollywood has provided us with plenty examples of how not to write a strong female character, I’m happy to say we also got one of my all time personal favorites with Shogun’s Toda Mariko. *SPOILERS AHOY* I’m a huge fan of the book by James Clavell. I read it as a teen, absolutely loved the character and I still think it’s one of the best I’ve ever come across. I am so grateful to the showrunners and cast for bringing her to life with such respect for the source material. So, what exactly makes her a great character with the particularity of being female? It’s the fact that her flaws and attributes make sense. Her strength is not physical. Yes, she can swing a spear around like the best of them, but she’s no match for the bigger, stronger male samurai. This is an expected flaw for a female character, and it’s one of the obstacle she has to overcome with her character traits. If this was written by Disney, she’d be eating a sandwich while killing all those guys, then headbutting the castle gate open. Her strength comes from her unwavering loyalty to her masters cause, her devotion to her religion, and her compassionate nature. Her sense of duty and her kindness are what drive her every move, never concerned with her own self. She goes down a path she knows damn well will lead to death, offering her life in service of a greater cause and finding time along the way to care for loved ones. Like making sure the Portuguese don’t murder Blackthorn after she’s gone. She is the very definition of a hero. Her weapons are not swords and spears, but courage and kindness. The courage to follow her masters suicidal orders, calling out the regents on their transgressions, and the kindness to forge long lasting friendships with anyone she comes across. It’s the combination of those that brought allies to Toranaga’s side, and ultimately won him the war. In line with that, her most badass scene is not the fight in the castle courtyard. It’s her speech in front of the regents: I am no peasant to be trotted on. I am daughter of the great Lord Akechi Jinsai. My line has been samurai for a thousand years, and I will never be captive, or hostage, or confined. Goosebumps

Name: Michael Strauss
Question: What is the most beautiful thing that you have ever seen?
Answer: The Northern Lights I’ve always been attracted to the natural wonders of the world. Maybe it’s my introverted side, but seeing a mountain top, or a quiet lake has always been more attractive to me than visiting any given city. The Aurora Borealis has been at the top of my bucket list for as long as I can remember. When me and my wife started dating, we decided to have one annual winter trip somewhere north of the arctic circle. A few days away from civilization, in some frozen piece of fairy tale land, waiting to catch a glimpse of this wonder of Mother Nature. This picture was taken on our third trip. After three days in a log cabin, in the frozen tundras of Lapland, the sky finally opened up and we saw it. I’ll never forget feeling so small and insignificant yet so at peace. I think of it every time I start taking myself too seriously.

Name: Michael Strauss
Question: What are your thoughts on the Trump assassination attempt?
Answer: I see three objective takeaways that any level headed person, on either side of the fence should be able to agree on. There is a lot to unpack, and a lot still unknown to the public. Mostly we can just speculate, but these points I can confidently say are undeniable for any decent, reasonable human being. First and foremost, an innocent bystander was killed. A horrible tragedy that will haunt his family for as long as they live. Regardless of political views, no sane person will try to frame this as anything else. People on social media who claim this was justified are either mentally unstable or just plan evil. 2. Trump’s reaction was impressive Love him or hate him, anyone who saw the footage should be able to admit that Trump acted like a badass. The guy’s reaction was otherworldly. He was shot at. A bullet took a piece of his ear. He was on the floor, with secret service agents scrambling all around him. In that commotion, he stood up. He raise his fist in the air, and screamed “FIGHT!” in a way that reassured an entire stadium full of panicking civilians. That’s a real life movie moment if ever I’ve seen one. I hear veterans saying people show their true colors when they are shot at. Whatever else Trump may be, he’s no coward. Anyone who looks at this and does not at least give an approving head nod, even if reluctant to do so, is not being genuine. 3. Polarization has gone too far The violence we are seeing is a logical conclusion, following years of increasing hate between the two sides. I’m not commenting on who is more or less guilty, as that is just speculation. What I am confident to say for sure is that both groups contributed to it. Civil discourse has gone out the window. Agree to disagree is a phrase of the past. Loud voices on each side keep screaming at each other, refusing to acknowledge the humanity across the fence, preferring in stead to increase the divide. There are liberals who openly lament over the failure of the attempt. There are republicans who refuse the olive branch of the more level headed democrats, who just want to say “ok, this is getting a little too far, isn’t it?” That attitude is wrong. As I said, a lot about what happened is speculative, and there can be a ton of complex viewpoints on many different topics, each with their own share of merit. These three points however are not debatable. I can confidently say that anyone who does not agree with them has been completely hijacked by their emotions. I will be cautious of anyone who is like that, both on and offline. I should add though, I’m a fairly optimistic person. I believe most voters are level headed people that will now be able to find some common ground. Hopefully they will work their way up from there.

Name: Michael Strauss
Question: What inaccuracies in movies really annoy you?
Answer: The use of data Pretty much anything that has to do with coding or science is treated like a magical plot device in Hollywood, but the use of data for me takes the cake. The minuscule effort needed to read, send and understand data is laughable. Even in the case of otherwise intelligent movies like Interstellar. Professor Brand said he can’t finish his gravity equation because he needs to process data found inside a black hole. A couple of hours of screen time later, Matthew Mcconaughey dives in, and starts sending this data to Murph. How is this raw data from a freaking black hole, that will “solve the problem of gravity” transferred you ask? Is it via some sort of sci-fi cloud based solution, that will allow Murph access to terrabytes worth of information to filter through? Nope. It’s morse code. Morse code. That she has to manually read from the spastic hands of her watch, and write down with pencil and paper. Like a Neanderthal. 90% of a data analyst’s job is finding the right data set, filtering it, cleaning it and processing it before they can even start to hope for some insight. I don’t know what kind of a minuscule, insignificant amount can be transferred via morse code, but I’m sure it doesn’t fit the use case. That to me is less believable than the whole space-time continuum bending part of the scene.

Name: Michael Strauss
Question: What are some examples of actors who have gone above and beyond in preparation for their roles in Hollywood?
Answer: Joaquin Phoenix - I’m still here Joaquin Phoenix almost detonated not just his career, but his entire public perception to play himself in I’m still here. The production features Joaquin Phoenix, giving up acting to pursue an ill advised rapping career. It follows Joaquin around, documenting his transformation from the successful and charismatic Hollywood actor to a mentally unstable, hobo-looking, laughing stock. The catch: this all happened under the public eye, with no one other than Joaquin and the producer knowing it’s fake. They wanted to capture the medias genuine reaction, and were very willing to make Joaquin look like he’s lost his mind for it. And so, with a straight face, Joaquin announced his retirement from acting in order to become a rap sensation. The press and public immediately assumed he’s having a meltdown. Phoenix announces his retirement in October 2008 and adopts his new persona – a scruffy, uncontrolled, and unstable version of himself, who turns out to be not particularly successful as a rapper. As his new identity is revealed to the audience, he becomes a target for public criticism and mockery. People are astonished: how could this have happened? Is this authentic? Is this real? He then continued the charade for two whole years, slowly chipping away at his public image. His personal hygiene looked on par with your average urban tent dweller, he was reported snorting cocaine and ordering hookers, he was making awkward appearances rapping in clubs and getting into altercations with hecklers. All these people think it’s for real The coup de grâce was an appearance on David Letterman in 2009 which, if you haven’t seen, I highly recommend. Joaquin shows up on the show, with David Letterman, his studio audience and so many live viewers in his hobo, mentally degraded alter-ego, with the specific intent of making a fool of himself! Again, no one is aware he is faking it. It’s the most awkward interview possible. Joaquin just sits there acting high on God knows what, while Letterman’s skills as a host are tested to the limits. He handled it masterfully, by the way. At some point, accepting he’s not getting anything from his guest, he just kind of starts taking jabs him. The interview ends with “Joaquin, I’m sorry you couldn’t be here tonight.” The ruse continued for an entire year after that. Pretty much everyone in the industry, media, and public was convinced he’d lost his marbles. No one was taking him seriously by this point. The producer was aware of this, but kept plowing ahead. Did Phoenix surprise you with how far he was willing to go? "Yeah, he did." … And then, with just seconds to go, I ask perhaps the most pertinent question of all: fake or not, is this his subject's attempt to destroy his celebrity image for good? "I don't think so," he says. "I really don't. I mean, it's a good question, but …" The big reveal in 2010 was suppose to undo all the damage. Unfortunately for him the movie was a flop. No one watched it. Many were left thinking he was just another celebrity that had a public meltdown and moved on without too much thought. He explained all this himself when he reappeared on Letterman afterwards. I certainly knew there was a risk. I’m not sure I have much of a career now Overall this was not a very smart career move and it’s impressive he was able to get back on track. Maybe an actual rap career would have been a better choice than this role. I do have to give him props though. To go on stage in front of so many people and purposely make an ass of yourself takes a whole new level of courage.

Name: Michael Strauss
Question: Have smart people ever acted dumb?
Answer: Stephen King Yes, all the time. It’s fascinating to see how successful, objectively smart people can act just as dimwitted and clueless as the rest of us. Take Stephen King for example. He is obviously a highly intelligent person who cemented himself as a giant in his respective craft. When it comes to his twitter activity though…cross out his name and you’d think you’re talking to a run of the mill troll. His composure is on par with your average teenage social recluse, venting frustrations and getting into flame wars with strangers. Here he is getting into it with Elon Musk and Dan Bongino. He’s not only reserving his insults for the high brow cliques though, he’s very inclusive. Here he is taking time out of his day to rage on a small, under 500 user account. Aside from regular flaming, he also likes to post over the top fear mongering tweets, coupled with generalizing, insulting blanket statements. I’m not commenting on his political stance, by the way. I’m commenting on the way these tweets are phrased. The outlandish claims, the insults, the condescending demeanor. This is not something you’d expect from an intellectual of his caliber. In light of terrible recent events, I can’t help but feel this attitude is only feeding the tension. Instead of a level headed approach, that can actually get people to listen, his tweets are more like something you’d expect from this lady. Finally, to remind us of that one annoying kid who always threatened to take his ball and go home, here he is threatening to leave twitter over ‘his principles’. He’s still raging away on tweeter, in spite of the subscription policy. To be fair, Elon did drop the price to $8. I guess the $12 saving makes up for his principles.

Name: Michael Strauss
Question: What are some famous movies based on novels that had a different ending than the novels they were based on?
Answer: The Mist (2007) The Mist is a science fiction horror film, inspired by the Stephen King 1980 novel with the same name. It’s the same source material that inspired one of the greatest video game series of all time. Still hanging from that cliff *SPOILERS AHOY* The movie is a pretty typical survival horror, but it does have one interesting claim to fame. One of the darkest endings in a Hollywood production. Surprisingly, this ending did not come from Stephen Kings novel, but from the screenwriters themselves. The films follows our protagonists David (Thomas Jane) and his son Billy (Nathan Gamble) trying to survive a sudden monster spawning mist that has covered the city. Hiding in a gas station with a bunch of other civilians, they eventually have to leave their shelter together with three other survivors. All the while being chased by weird things. Their car breaks down in the middle of a wooded area, monster noises all around, covered by the hellish mist. Feeling a brutal death is unavoidable, they all decide it’s easier to commit suicide then and there. David, who only has four bullets in his gun, decides to do the noble thing. He kills the four passengers, including his own son, and steps outside to be torn to bits by the alien creatures. And then this happens: Yep. The noises were actually the cavalry coming to the rescue. David collapses to the ground, now having to live with the thought of killing four people including HIS OWN SON for nothing. The end. I personally don’t like the ending. It’s only purpose is to shock and make the viewer feel terrible, without any subtext. I can appreciate a meaningful tragic end, but this was just pointlessly nihilistic. Still, as far a shock value goes, it’s one of the best. Even coming from Stephen King himself: "It was so anti-Hollywood — anti-everything, really! It was nihilistic. I liked that" Yes, coming from him, this is a compliment.

Name: Michael Strauss
Question: What movies can you watch all the time and never get tired of watching?
Answer: Snatch (2000) This 2000 crime comedy, while not exactly my all time favorite movie, is definitely the one I have re-watched the most. It’s my favorite iteration of the one movie Guy Ritchie kept trying to make over and over again. I have a habit of getting people unfamiliar with it to sit down and watch it, which means I usually stay to police them. As annoying as that sounds, no one complained so far. They all sit down kicking and screaming but get soothed 10 minutes into the film, surrendering to the British humor, zany characters and captivating cinematography. If you haven’t this movie, and like a gritty comedy that will have you laughing one moment and pinned to the edge of your seat the next, I highly recommend you watch this. It also features a great cast with - among others - Brad Pitt, Jason Statham, Alan Ford, Dennis Farina, Vinnie Jones and a squeaking Bull Terrier.

Name: Michael Strauss
Question: Can you recommend a lesser-known comedy-horror movie that you enjoy? What makes it stand out to you?
Answer: The Babysitter (2017) - spoiler free This production is one of my favorite comedies in recent years. It’s a black, teen comedy that features a talented cast of actors, an enjoyable coming of age story and a slew of well crafted comedy moments one can enjoy IF AND ONLY IF they have a good stomach for gore. Generic 12 year old, the nerdy misfit Cole (Judah Lewis) is left under the supervision of his hot but equally nerdy babysitter/best friend Bee (Samara Weaving) for the night. Tricking her into thinking he’s asleep, Cole sneaks outside his bedroom to spy on her, as she invites over her group of friends to play spin the bottle. To Cole’s surprise, the flirty game soon turns into a human sacrifice ritual meant to contact Satan. The rest of the movie is basically a game of cat and mouse, where instead of Tom and Jerry you have a 12 year old boy and a bunch of deranged cultists. One of the things I enjoyed most about the film is the balance between Coles coming of age arc and the horror movie background. Comedies in this genre tend to sacrifice the former in favor of shock and gore elements, but I find The Babysitter does a fine job caring for both. The dynamic between the main characters is well scripted and acted, to the point it actually got me invested, in spite of one of them being a homicidal Satan worshipper. The supporting cast does a great job as well, providing us with plenty moments of comedic relief on one hand, and chill inducing terror on the other. The humor ranges from absurd, to subtle, to juvenile, with each angle being well crafted and delivered. Even the gore is made in such an over the top, silly way that I was half squirming, half laughing every time it came up. I really enjoyed the pacing of the show as well. The first part introduces the characters and does a great job bringing us into Cole’s world. Full of movies, games, and a general sense of childish innocence. Then we have the second part, bursting in like an axe wielding Jack Nicholson. The change of tone was so abrupt, I was laughing at the sheer absurdity of the contrast. I have to warn again about the gore though. It’s not for the squeamish. If you can tolerate that, then this is a fun movie.

Name: Michael Strauss
Question: What are engineers tired of explaining?
Answer: Probabilities The concept of uncertainty seems to be foreign to the general public. Say for example, removing cards out of a deck. If the first four cards are black, and you need to bet on what color the fifth card is, the correct bet would be red. There is a chance it will be black again, but the correct bet is on red. Say I bet on red, justifying it by using probabilities. Say I lose. Every insecure weasel in a 10 km radius will show up to tell me how my decision was wrong, and how I as an engineer should have known better. To make a point that knowing the probability of an event is irrelevant, since either outcomes can happen. To them, anything less than 100% certainty is not to be considered. They will hold this one incident as proof, and die on that hill if they need to. Ignoring the fact that if we repeat this experiment 100 times, I will win more than I will lose. Many people cannot wrap their heads around a decision still being correct, in spite of a bad outcome. Anything that is not 0% or 100% likely is an element of chaos. I feel it has a sort of belief system component to it, almost like a religious angle. I imagine most people like to think the world is deterministic. Input A always results in output B. The world makes sense, and if you make the right decisions, good outcomes will happen. The concept of probabilities, of a stochastic world, says “yes, for the most part…sometimes though, you do everything right, but sh*t just doesn’t go your way”. People don’t like that.

Name: Michael Strauss
Question: What is the worst name for a rock band?
Answer: Mötley Crüe almost had one of the worst names ever. Yes, one of the coolest, most quintessential 80’s rock bands was toying with the name Christmas. The newly formed band did not yet have a name. Neil has said that he told his bandmates that he was "thinking about calling the band Christmas". The other members were not very receptive to that idea. This little snipped of dialogue from the Netflix documentary The Dirt pretty much sums up that idea: Nikki Sixx: “We can use all the Jesus imagery, it’s got shock value.” Mick Mars: “Yeah. I’m shocked by how much it blows.”

Name: Michael Strauss
Question: What is the most racist film ever?
Answer: Eurotrip In 2004, DreamWorks released a teen comedy which follows a bunch of U.S. kids traveling through Europe. Only, instead of a showcase of the rich history and cultural background of the countries we go through, we get a shameless mockery of as many negative stereotypes as the showrunners could cram in the 93 minutes runtime. I realize I’m not using the word “racist” in the traditional sense for this answer, but the definition of that word has been so twisted and bent out of shape lately that I feel perfectly comfortable fitting it here. The movie follows around Scott (Scott Mechlowicz) and his friends Cooper (Jacob Pitts), Jamie (Travis Wester) and Jenny (Michelle Trachtenberg) in their quest to find Scott’s pen pal and would be future girlfriend Mieke, who lives in Berlin. The first stop in our Euro adventure is London. We get to meet the locals: violent soccer hooligans. Featuring Vinnie Jones just being himself The kids befriend them by pretending to be Manchester United fans and manage to hitch a ride on their - you guessed it - double decker bus to France. Here, Vinnie introduces us to the next stop in our offensive stereotype exhibition. In France, our group of teens decides to visit a nudist beach, only to find out that it’s full of naked old men. Once the men see Jenny - the only girl on the beach - they immediately start chasing her while shouting “Girl!” like in a Pepé Le Pew cartoon. You know, like any red blooded french man would. There’s a baguette joke in there somewhere On one of their train rides, the hilarious Fred Armisen makes a cameo. He plays a role simply referred to as “creepy italian guy”. True to his character, he joins the kids in their compartment, scoots in between them, and gropes them every time the train goes through a tunnel. He pretends it’s all a misunderstanding but keeps getting more and more rapey with every tunnel. Next we make a stop in Eastern Europe. More specifically in Bratislava. Could have been filmed in modern L.A. Here we have horror music in the background, dirty hobos washing themselves on the streets and dogs playing with dismembered human body parts. The kids are down to under $2 in total budget, but that still gets them the finest luxury hotels, massages and restaurants. Because Eastern Europe is a dump where having any amount of U.S. money makes you rich. Finally, our heroes reach Germany. They get to Mieke’s house, where they are greeted by her parents and her little brother, who likes to play with sharpies. He also likes playing pretend. So there you go. A picture of Europe, all reduced to it’s most offensive stereotypes. I feel I should add, I thought this movie was hilarious and I recommend it if you are looking for a silly, no brain comedy. I saw it multiple times with my friends as a teen, even though my country was one of the targets of the show. We did not mind that one bit. The movie is not trying to generalize or make any political statements. It’s simply seizing an opportunity for comedy by exploiting a bunch of stereotypes. The humor itself does not come from suggesting these stereotypes are true, but from how ridiculously over the top they are portrayed. I feel we could use more of that. Negative stereotypes lose their power when we stop taking them seriously and allow ourselves to joke about them.

Name: Michael Strauss
Question: Should one start by reading 'Game of Thrones' or watching the TV series?
Answer: Neither I hate to be this guy. Honestly. But this is what being a fan of ASOIAF did to me. When I started reading the books, people were telling me “why bother? George R.R. Martin will never finish the story. He’s way too invested in his HBO deals, he’s getting a ton of money and stopped caring about the book”. I used to call these people cynical. “You’re a dumbass”, I would say, like the sweet summer child I was. “The care he has for his story is beyond anything money can bring. Material gain doesn’t distract such a creative mind from finishing their life’s work. I feel bad for anyone who thinks otherwise.” I can honestly say those books are unlike anything I ever read. I never thought a story can take me on such a roller coaster of emotions. Soaring through the sky at one moment and drowning in the mud in the next. I was so invested, I was only watching seasons of the show once I had finished the respective book. Soon after the show went beyond, I stopped watching altogether. I did everything I needed to avoid spoilers, waiting for the next book to come out. Can you imagine the level of vigilance I needed? GoT was the single most discussed topic anywhere you went. On the internet and in real life, people were discussing the latest episodes as if their lives depended on it. It was the new weather talk. That show cured awkward elevator rides. I had to completely go off the internet. For all my friends, I would answer the phone with “Please don’t talk about Game of Thrones!”. I stopped going to social events altogether. Eventually I had to live in a cave, away from civilization, surviving off rainwater, tree bark and small rodents. Any minute now! Ok, I’m exaggerating, but this next part is true: I still have not seen the last two seasons, I have no idea how it ends, or what happened to my favorite characters. I read those books 13 years ago. 13 years! As much as I loved them, I forgot more than half the plot points. If by some miracle “Winds of Winter” does come out, I’d have to reread the previous two books just to get back on track. And then what? George R.R. Martin said (13 years ago!) he anticipates at least 2 more volumes. Does that mean I have to wait another decade and go through the same exercise again? Not to mention he is 75 years old and not exactly the pinnacle of physical health. Him publishing another volume at 88 is not very likely. It saddens me to no end, but I finally give in and accept the reality: A Song of Ice And Fire will never be finished. What bugs me the most is not the obscenely long waiting time between publications. Or the fact that I feel cheated as a fan and a consumer. It’s the fact that George R.R. Martin seems to have given up on it completely. He spent the last years (13 of them!) getting sidetracked by HBO, writing prequels, histories and books with parallel stories and maps of Westeros. In his mind, the passion for ASOIAF is probably already done. It’s not worth investing in these books if the author himself checked out. So much investment only to be left hanging. Emotionally blue-balled, if you will. And as for the series, everyone is saying the last two seasons were a complete let down. I hear this meme sums it up pretty well

Name: Michael Strauss
Question: What movie has been shot but has never been shown? Why?
Answer: Batgirl (2022) Between 2017 and 2022, DC films was busy with the production of a Batgirl movie that ended up as a $90 million piece of memorabilia, collecting dust in a locked vault, never to see the light of day. The sad part is, this movie actually sounded good. There’s no obvious reason why it should not have been a success, at least looking from the outside. Aside for a few alignment issues between the film directors (Adil El Arbi and Bilall Fallah) and the studio CEO (Walter Hamada), the films development seemed to be going smoothly. It was on schedule, on budget, and for the most part free of studio interference and outside controversies. The screenplay, written by Christina Hudson (Birds of Prey), was less focused on high budget blockbuster action and more on delivering a gritty, character centered story about Barbara Gordon’s (Leslie Grace) search for the man that killed her mother in an arson attack. An interesting premise that would have brought Michael Keaton back in the role of Batman, J.K. Simmons as James Gordon, and Brendan Frasier as the big bad of the movie, Firefly. I feel like that cast alone was enough to get moviegoers curious. At least to see how Michael Keaton’s Batman holds up today, or to see Brendan Frasier’s resurging career. Or if they can take J.K. Simmons seriously in any other superhero movie role than this guy: Alas, in 2022, DC was struggling after a series of failed projects and decided to change a bunch of it’s senior executives, including the CEO, who was replaced with David Zaslav. Zaslav took one look at the DCEU, decided it was an out of control clusterf*ck that needs a hard reset - which…fair enough - and cancelled pretty much all ongoing projects to write them off as tax breaks. Batgirl included.

Name: Michael Strauss
Question: What is the saddest villain death in any series?
Answer: Thor - God of War Ragnarok *SPOILERS AHOY* The representation of Thor in the God of War upside down but brilliant version of Scandinavian mythology is probably the coolest I’ve seen in any modern piece of entertainment, in spite of his tragic arc. That’s probably why I found his death so sad. We only get to see him in the second installment of the game, after hearing many tales of his strength and cruelty, and witnessing the aftermath of his bloody, genocidal rampage that all but wiped out the giants. The slow buildup, the inevitability of conflict, and his intro scene - menacingly towering over Kratos as he walks into his home - are an introduction worthy of the mighty God of Thunder. As despicable and threatening as Thor is introduced to be, he soon becomes a tragic character that I couldn’t help but feel bad for. We get glimpse into his life when Atreus joins Odin’s quest of finding the Mask artifact. After coming back from a mission, the following dialogue sums up the dynamic between Thor and his father: Atreus: Thor was great, I learned a lot from him. Odin: You learned something from him? Really now? Okay, what did you teach the kid? Thor: Nothing. What could I possibly teach him. Odin: Exactly. (Thor leaves) Atreus: You always this hard on Thor? Odin: It’s nothing like that. It’s the only language he understands. I’m serious. Go ahead, try being nice to him. See where that gets you. The theme of parenthood is present all through the game, and is explored via multiple angles. Unfortunately for Thor, he is stuck with the neglectful and abusive side. He respects and obeys his father, although he has treated him like a rabid dog his entire life. Constantly berating to keep him submissive, and to make him the vicious killing machine he is. To Odin, Thor is not a son. He is a weapon. Any independent thought or feeling from him is just the sign of a malfunctioning tool that needs fixing. Nothing more. “Are you talking? Who told you to do that? You don’t talk. You don’t think. I think, you kill. It’s a simple f*cking concept!” - father of the year material. Thor’s inability to go against Odin causes him to be riddled with frustration, guilt and shame in front of his own wife (Sif) and daughter (Thrud), who clearly see what this dysfunctional relationship is doing to him. We see little glimpses of him trying to break free, but is unable to overcome his childhood programming. He then turns to drinking, which further grows the divide between him and his daughter. As it often happens in the real world, his fathers crappy parenting is now affecting his own child. “Let it be known the God of Thunder is good at two things: killing giants and pissing mead!” - Thor voicing out his trauma and pathological response, right before starting a bar fight in front of his concerned daughter. This is followed up by a really sad scene. Thor, too drunk to move on his own, is carried out of the bar by Atreus and Thrud. He collapses by the side of the bar. His daughter is begging him to get up, saying she is there for him, but Thor is so eaten away by shame that he can’t even look at her. This whole development is sad enough, especially since it’s all so real and relatable, but the worst part is his last scene. We get to the final boss fights, Kratos and Thor square off. Kratos comes on top but decides to spare Thor. The fight ends with this dialogue: Thor: “What the f*ck are you waiting for?!” Kratos (helping Thor get up): “Your daughter. My son calls her friend.” Thor: “Don’t you know what I’ve done?” Kratos: “Yes! But what will you do now?” Thor (picking up Mjolnir): “We don’t change. We… are destroyers” Kratos (sheathing his axe): “No more. For the sake of our children, we must be better.” That’s when things finally fall into place for Thor. He sees how he allowed Odin’s abuse to turn him into a monster and a terrible father to his own children. He understands from Kratos’s example that change is possible. He walks away, refusing to be Odin’s mindless weapon anymore. He lays down Mjolnir in protest. And then this happens: Without the slightest hesitation, Odin kills him. In front of his own daughter. The tool has malfunctioned, and there’s nothing left but to throw it into the garbage. I’m a big fan of redemption stories and a big believer in second chances. What makes this the saddest villain death for me is that Thor was ready to correct himself. Just like Kratos, he had a dark past, full of unspeakable acts. Also like Kratos, he was now ready to turn away from that past and walk a path of redemption. To become better for the sake of his family and those around him. Unlike Kratos though, he never got the chance.

Question: What are some scenes in movies that went wrong but were left in the film?
Answer: “I’m walking here” - Midnight Cowboy This is one of the most quotable lines in movie history, even for those who never saw Midnight Cowboy. Joe (John Voight) and Ratso (Dustin Hoffman) are crossing a busy New York street, when Ratso is almost hit by a cab. Ratso bangs on the hood of the car, aggressively screaming “I’m walking here!” as the guy drives away. Turns out that was not supposed to be in the movie. Dustin Hoffman was actually almost hit by a cab that passed a red light. He stayed in character and delivered one of the most iconic lines in cinema, while perfectly capturing his character and the tone of the movie. Here’s Hoffman describing how it happened: It was a low-budget movie. Nobody wanted to make this movie, Midnight Cowboy. People walked out during previews; it was considered filthy in 1969. Very low budget. Consequently, on Sixth Avenue, there was no money to stack it with extras. So it’s what they call a stolen shot. We have radio mikes on, the van is across the street, we rehearse it by ourselves. You know, the director [John Schlesinger], me and [Jon] Voight. And we would have to do this dialogue walking. And the hidden camera across the street would go with us, but we couldn’t stop the signal, so we had to reach the dialogue at a certain point so we wouldn’t have to stop. It would have to be turning green when we hit it. So we rehearsed it ourselves and we finally got — oh, so we’ll start this far back, then we’ll do this pace and then we’ll get there when it just hits green — perfect — and we can just continue. And we do it, and the first take a cab jumps the light … I wound up saying, ‘I’m walkin’ here!’ But what was going through my head is: ‘Hey, we’re makin’ a movie here! And you just f–ked this shot up.’ But somehow something told me you’d better keep it within the character.

Name: Michael Strauss
Question: The movie Furiosa just flopped despite rave reviews from Rotten Tomatoes and film critics. Why are film critics/enthusiasts often so out of touch with what general audiences want to see in a film?
Answer: Misplaced apathy Furiosa is the collateral victim of an ill advised, deliberate audience alienating marketing campaign Hollywood has been conducting for more than a decade now. There are plenty of reasons coming together to create the recent string of flopping projects initially expected to be hits (Furiosa, The Fall Guy, Kingdom of the Planet of the Apes), but the one I want to elaborate on is the cloud of apathy covering the general moviegoers crowd. To explain this point, I first have to give a short summary of Hollywood’s more recent marketing schemes and how they terribly and predictably backfired. For the better part of the last decade, in a majority of cases concerning popular action, adventure and fantasy franchises, studio executives decided it’s not right for their predominant viewership to be male. To correct this travesty, they proudly initiated a string of projects and aggressive marketing campaigns meant to skew the viewer demographic more towards a female audience. We got the president of Marvel Studios saying the MCU will have more female than male superheroes[1], the president of Lucas Films complaining that Star Wars is underperforming due to the fanbase being too male dominated[2]and calling for more female representation[3], we have newer shows like The Witcher altering the source material to shift more focus on female characters[4]and the list goes on. Now, there is nothing wrong with expanding to new demographics and increasing female lead roles per se. That’s a decision that makes perfect sense. However, it quickly becomes clear the goal was not to expand to new demographics, it was to replace the existing one. Two actions were taken in parallel, one more successful than the other. Alienating the male audience On one side, studios started moving away from male moviegoers by injecting preachiness and male hating rhetoric in a bunch of projects, with a special target on franchises popular with the demographic. Writers started peppering movies with lines about how masculinity is toxic and how men are oppressive, inferior creatures that need to “do better”. We have the new female Dr. Who referring to her gender as “an upgrade”, we have Batgirl saying the batsuit will only be perfect “when it fits a woman”, we have She Hulk with the superpower of complaining about men every other line of her entire show, and many more. We even got a ton of legacy shattering prequels, sequels and reboots that either make the original male characters look like complete idiots or replace them with female counterparts. Han Solo is now a deadbeat dad who needs Ray to show him how operate his own ship, Indiana Jones is a sad old man who gets outsmarted by Helena at every step, and pretty much every male Marvel superhero is playing second fiddle to their female counterparts while being reduced to walking punchlines. On top of this, producers and actors adjacent to these projects got directives to make their reluctance towards male viewers clear with every chance they got. It became very common in interviews to state how proud everyone is to be moving away from them. Everything “non-male” was marketed as a sign of evolution. Mind you this is for the more classy cases. The less classy, well…we have the self proclaimed activist director of upcoming Star Wars Rey movie saying “I love to make men uncomfortable” or Captain Marvel’s Brie Larson saying “I don’t need a 40 year old white dude telling me what they think, it’s not for them”. All in all, the vibe has been unnecessarily mean towards male fans. Of course, not all studios are partaking in this (more on that later), but the guilty parties are responsible for some of the most popular franchises ever and cover a major part of Hollywood output. The tone they set quickly contaminates everything in the space. After years of hammering it home, the message was finally received. Male audiences became apathetic or downright defensive. Their assumption became that any new project from popular action adventure franchises is deliberately made to be unappealing to them. This part of the plan worked. Part two however was not so successful. Attracting a larger female audience Once the men have safely been removed from the premises, studios went on to filling the now open seats with female viewers. The plan for that was simple. Good old fashion pandering. They started creating more and more female characters, gender swapping old male ones and started spreading the word that these franchises - which were never gendered, by the way - now belong to women. The acting, writing, directing and production staffs have been made more and more “female centered”. That is not a negative on it’s own. The issue however is that this was the main and often times only focus point of the marketing campaigns: we have women in our show, so women will flock to see them regardless of quality, was the logic. I’m not sure if this level of pandering is more or less insulting then what they did to their male audience, but that is a topic for another answer. The point is, it didn’t work. Take The Marvels for example. All female cast, all female writing staff and female director. On paper, it was the completion of this grand masterplan. The moment when superhero movie audiences become predominantly female. The Marvels lost $237 million[5]. And here’s the kicker. 68% of the audience was still male[6]. The same thing happened over and over again, with most Disney’s Star Wars movies[7], Madame Web[8], Doctor Who[9], The Witcher[10], The Rings of Power[11], and pretty much any project that adhered to this disastrous strategy. The funny part is, even after the data was in, many refuse to see what was right in front of them. This tweet from one of Jimmy Fallon’s writers pretty much sums up the attitude of many in Hollywood: Of course it’s the consumers fault Many turned to their favorite hobby - crapping on potential male fans. In a fascinating feat of mental gymnastics, men are to blame for the failure of these movies even though they still make up more than 50% of the audience[12]. The failure of shows geared to appeal to women are failing because men are not supporting them more. At no point during this backpedaling has the lack of female viewers ever been brought up, which takes me to my next point. Demographics The demographics of different movie genres has to do with inherent preferences, and is not something that can be socially engineered in an impactful way. Women will not flock to see a movie from a genre they are not interested in to begin with just because the lead and director are female. Action adventure movies skew towards male audiences, just how romantic comedies and musicals skew towards female ones. There is as much chance of creating a predominantly female audience for action movies as you have of creating a predominantly straight male audience for Barbie or Fifty Shades of Grey. It’s a fools errand, and Hollywood’s activitst experiment proves it. The male audience has been put off, while the female audience is made up of the same women that were happy going to see Iron Man and The Phantom Menace. To sum up, in what will probably go down as the most counterproductive movement in the history of any entertainment industry, Hollywood successfully alienated well over 50% of their audience and did nothing of note to expand on the remaining one. Now, you might say “if these movies were actually well written, people would have gone to see them”. Fully agreed! But the majority of the audience would still be male, as will always be the case with action adventure franchises. And speaking of well written movies: This finally brings me to Furiosa. This is a well written, well acted movie with a compelling story and world build that would delight almost anyone who is interested in the genre, and beyond. There is no obvious reason why it should flop. It’s actually one of the few recent examples where both critics and audiences agree. The reason it flopped is not because it’s not a good movie. It’s because audiences did not even give it a chance. The average moviegoer saw the trailer, saw what looked like another popular franchise getting rebooted with a gender-swapped lead, and decided it’s likely another legacy shattering, pandering piece of activist material that is not made for their genuine entertainment. Add the increased ticket price and the convenience of streaming services and it’s easy to see why many people thought it’s not worth the risk. I will reiterate, Furiosa is a good movie. The movie itself and the marketing leading up to it are not guilty of any of the sins I listed above. It’s just an innocent victim, caught in the blast radius of an activist marketing stunt carried out by others in the same space. And it’s a damn shame.

Question: What do introverts dislike about extroverts?
Answer: The assumption that introverts are too shy to talk “We are a team that fosters diversity and inclusion” my new manager opened up our team workshop. “In that spirit, I ask the more extroverted members to leave space so that the more introverted ones can also speak up. I know it is harder for them to do so, and I would like us all to be mindful of that” she added. In unison, all the extroverts turned to me and three other introverts, smiling and nodding their heads, like we are special needs cases who haven’t mastered the basic social skill of talking to people. For the remainder of the 8 hour workshop, people would pause, look directly at me and the other special needs employees and ask “would you like to add something?”. I did not sign up for this I was recently hired in the group, so it felt I was required to match the tone by giving long winded inputs in corporate speak*. That’s not easy for an introvert. Creating elaborate answers about things we don’t genuinely care about is very draining. A few hours in, as I was getting more and more depleted, so were my answers getting shorter. Soon, I was only responding with “Nope, nothing from me”. Some were giving me looks as if I was downright rude, but I was beyond the point where I could fake it. I was just trying to get through this thing. Now, I understand this attitude is coming from a good place. I like extroverts. Most of my close friends are extroverts. My wife is one of the most extroverted people I ever met. Yes, our relationship dynamic works great. But they can not wrap their heads around someone just choosing to not speak. Of simply not having anything to say. To them, the only reason to stay quiet is either you are protesting the conversation or you are too shy to speak up, in which case you need special help. That bugs me to no end. The assumption that I am a shy, social recluse and the patronizing attempts to lure me in with smiles and gentle head nods. Like a squirrel your trying to feed without scaring away. Introverts do not feel the need to regularly bring the spotlight on them. If we are to take several minutes out of an entire teams time, then we make sure we are adding something new and valuable. It’s not because we don’t care, or because we don’t know how to speak, it’s because we are trying to optimize. It’s our way of being respectful of others time. It does not mean we are shy. We actually like having chatty extroverts in corporate meetings. They fill up all the awkward pauses, give managers the feedback they desperately want, and spare us the pressure having to bull*hit our way through an 8 hour workshop that we were forced to participate in. Speak up all you want, no introvert will be offended by that. *corporate speak - a manner of talking which involves speaking a lot of words without actually saying anything. Often used in the corporate world for the goal of getting attention, faking seniority and/or deflecting questions. See also ‘political speak’

Name: Michael Strauss
Question: Did Greek gods have sex?
Answer: Oh yes, this was a major plot device. A good part of Greek mythology starts with Zeus not being able to keep it in his pants. Any attractive female, be it mortal, goddess or titan, was fair game. He did seem to have one restriction though. He would sleep with pretty much anyone but his wife, Hera. It makes a bit of sense, she was also his sister, but that did not stop her from becoming jealous. When Zeus spotted a woman he wanted to sleep with, he had the habit of disguising himself in whatever person, creature or meteorological event would seduce her the easiest. He disguised himself as Alkmene’s husband to impregnate her with Heracles. Or as a golden shower, to impregnate Danae with Perseus. Here he is as a swan, getting it on with the Queen of Sparta. Castor and Pollux would be the result. A good number of mythological heroes and even gods were born from Zeus’s uncontrolled lust. After that, they would spend most of their lives fending off Hera’s jealous wrath, who would curse them and do everything in her power to make their lives miserable. Her revenge attempts were rarely directed at Zeus, but at his innocent, bastard children. Being a demigod is not all it’s cracked up to be when the most powerful goddess in Olympus makes it her mission to make your life a living hell. Greek mythology is tragic. And a lot of that tragedy, just like in real life, starts with poor impulse control.

Question: What is the most memorable ad-lib in movie history?
Answer: Life of Brian - Biggus Dickus scene This iconic Monty Python scene starts with an escort of roman guards bringing the captive Brian (Graham Chapman) in front of Rome’s governor Pontius Pilate (Michael Palin). The tone of the scene is already set by the juvenile jokes around Pontius Pilates’s lisp, which has the characters asking what after every sentence. It’s foreshadowing the kind of silly, teenage humor that at some point gets every 15 year old in trouble at school for giggling uncontrollably in inappropriate situations. Brian is accused of being a “Jewish rapscallion”. He defends himself saying this is all a mistake, that he is roman. He mentions his father was a roman centurion named Naughtius Maximus. The head guard laughs at the made up sounding name, but Pontius remains very serious. He does not see anything unusual with Naughtius Maximus. The guard explains it has to be a joke name, since it sounds like something a 12 year old class clown would come up with, like Sillius Soddus or Biggus Dickus. Pontius still doesn’t get it. “What’s so funny about Biggus Dickus”, he asks in a serious tone. “I have a great friend in Rome name Biggus Dickus”, to which one of the guards lets out a muffled chuckle. And this is where the improv starts. It turns out, the extras playing the guards were specifically instructed to not laugh under any circumstance! If they break, they do not get payment. So the silent giggles are all real. That’s Michael Palin’s cue. Like a hawk, he starts walking around the set, looking for vulnerable extras to try and get them to break. Comedian versus extras in an epic tug of war, and it is hilarious! Muffled giggles all around, Palin getting in their faces, all the while trying to not laugh himself. One of the extras even has to bite his cheeks, barely hanging on. At the end of the scene, Pontius brings up the fact that Biggus Dickus has a wife. Everyone is geared up for another ridiculously juvenile name. And right when he reveals the name Incontinentia Buttocks, the extras get a cue from the director and are allowed to burst out into laughter, which they immediately do, wrapping up a scene that is equal parts brilliant and ridiculous at the same time. I feel I should add, everything I wrote above is based on a bunch of internet sources and rumors, however I could not find any confirmation from the actor, aside from the fact that he himself had a very hard time filming this without cracking. The most difficult thing to shoot was the Pontius Pilate scene. All the centurions had to be on the verge of cracking up, while Graham and I had to remain totally straight-faced. I may be biased, but I like to think it’s true. How many of us in our childhood have not been in a situation similar to these extras? Trying not to laugh at a stupid joke, that is only made funny by the fact that we are in a serious setting, like a classroom or a ceremony? Trying not to break under the eyes of a stern teacher or parent? I love how it captures that feeling. It still has me giggling like a dumb teenager every time I watch it.

Name: Michael Strauss
Question: What are some shocking implications in movies nobody talks about?
Answer: The diversity introduced in The Rings of Power means there is a genocide coming up When Amazon ambitiously set out to create a prequel to The Lord of the Rings, one of the major focus points of the showrunners was to diversify the cast. They proudly set out to “correct” the wrongs of the original trilogy - which was full of white men - and filled up Tolkien's universe with modern day, U.S. minorities. This was even a big selling point leading up to the release of season one, with cast members and producers eagerly promoting the groundbreaking leap they just took in television history. For the first time ever in a fantasy show, we now have humans, elves and dwarves of different skin colors, all mixing and matching like in a modern day California. That’s ignoring The Witcher of course, but that’s a rival streaming service, so we pretend it doesn’t exist. Now, I have no issue with diversity per se, but in this particular case it has some sinister implications. If we are to accept this show happens in the same universe as Peter Jackson’s trilogy, then something terrible has to happen for Middle Earth to go from the diverse picture I posted above, to the very monochrome one we originally got. There are still 5 different races portrayed here I’m curious if Amazon will address this issue in later seasons, I’d be very interested to see what they come up with. Maybe we’ll have a season about The Great Cleansing of Middle Earth. Or The Great Gentrification, where rich white hobbits move into The Shire, raising prices and forcing out all the poor minority hobbits.

Name: Michael Strauss
Question: Who's a video game boss you didn't want to kill?
Answer: Máttugr Helson - God of War Máttugr Helson is the guardian of the Bridge of the Damned in the Scandinavian chapter of the God of War series. He’s basically the bouncer of Helheim, watching over the realm of the dead. He makes sure the living do not get in, and the dead do not get out. What made me feel bad about killing him is that Máttugr did nothing to deserve it. In a world of scheming, backstabbing gods - where a good part of them want to kill Kratos and Atreus - Máttugr is one of the few neutral creatures. He does not get involved in others business, he just does his role in keeping the balance of the realm. We can’t have the living and the dead mixing all willy nilly, and Máttugr is to thank for that. Unfortunately for him, Kratos’s son is afflicted by a disease that can only be cured with an elixir made from the bridge keeper’s heart. Innocent or not, Kratos has no choice but to kill him. I never questioned the decision to do so, but it still felt wrong. The whole fight I was thinking he can not surrender, bargain, or run away. The purpose was not to get passed him, it was to kill him. Finally, to add insult to injury, you take out his heart and leave his lifeless corpse on the bridge like run of the mill roadkill. I felt bad for the guy.
